newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Thai premier visits Vietnam to boost relations.
newsitem.headline: Thai premier visits Vietnam to boost relations.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh arrived in Vietnam on Sunday for a 24-hour visit to promote trade and economic ties and iron out long-standing differences over maritime boundaries and fishing rights.
Chavalit was greeted in a downpour of rain by Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet as he arrived at Hanoi's grand Presidential Palace.
A line of girls in traditional dress waved bouquets of flowers, a military band struck up and then the two premiers walked together over red carpet for an inspection of the guard.

Chavalit, on his third official visit to the communist country but his first as prime minister, told the Vietnam News Agency (VNA) last week that maritime sovereignty disputes were "a minor irritant" in overall good relations.
Clashes have long been common in the Gulf of Thailand, where the Thai and Vietnamese continental shelves overlap for about 6,000 sq km (2.300 sq miles).

Fishermen from both sides have been detained and their boats seized in the past for incursions into territory each country claims as its own. However, all fishermen have been released on both sides in recent months.

Diplomats said Chavalit, who was due to meet Secretary General of the Communist Party Do Muoi after his talks with Kiet, was paving the way for joint committee meetings on the disputes amd on bilateral cooperation in Hanoi in early May.
They said Chavalit and Kiet would also address the question of how to boost trade between the two countries.
VNA said two-way trade rose by $100 million in 1996 to $610 million and was expected to reach the $1.0-billion-dollar mark this year.
Thailand also ranks nineteenth in a list of foreign investors in Vietnam, committing about $1.2 billion for 74 projects.
Vietnam and Thailand, which normalised diplomatic relations in 1976, are both members of the seven-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
Hanoi recently called in ambassadors from ASEAN nations to brief them on its row with Beijing over Chinese drilling for oil in a South China Sea area that both sides claim.
